STALE_QUOTE def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation/boundary empty: items/def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation.md Definition; expected "Fix an integer $n\\ge1$, a canonical chart with physical coordinates $q_i$ in metres and $p_i$ in $\\mathrm{kg\\,m\\,s^{-1}}$, and the corresponding dimensionless coordinates $\\hat q_i=q_i/(1\\,\\mathrm m)$ and $\\hat p_i=p_i/(1\\,\\mathrm{kg\\,m\\,s^{-1}})$. Let $O\\subseteq\\mathbb R^{2n}$ be the open domain of the numerical vector $\\hat x=(\\hat q,\\hat p)$, let $\\hat H:O\\to\\mathbb R$ be the numerical energy map with physical energy $H=(1\\,\\mathrm J)\\hat H$, and require $\\hat H$ to have continuous partial derivatives through order two. A specified open interval $J_E\\subseteq\\mathbb R$ is a regular compact-shell band when $\\hat H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\\subset J_E$ and $\\nabla\\hat H$ is nonzero at every point of $\\hat H^{-1}(J_E)$.\n\nFor $\\hat E\\in J_E$, the energy shell is $\\Sigma_{\\hat E}:=\\{x\\in O:\\hat H(x)=\\hat E\\}$. The graph-chart definition of the weighted shell integral is [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]: in a local graph chart $x_i=h(z,\\hat E)$, its coarea measure is $d\\mu_{\\hat E}=dA_{\\hat E}/|\\nabla\\hat H|$, with graph-area factor and gradient in the dimensionless Euclidean coordinates. Set $D(\\hat E):=\\int_{\\Sigma_{\\hat E}}d\\mu_{\\hat E}$ and admit the preparation only when $\\Sigma_{\\hat E}\\ne\\varnothing$ and $0<D(\\hat E)<\\infty$. Its normalized shell law is $\\nu_{\\hat E}(A):=D(\\hat E)^{-1}\\mu_{\\hat E}(A\\cap\\Sigma_{\\hat E})$. The current draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]] proves the coarea identity, chart independence and positive finite shell mass under its stated $C^2$, compact-regular-band hypotheses; its statement and proof are present, while its acceptance remains unresolved. Multiplying the unnormalized shell measure by a fixed positive phase-volume normalization does not change $\\nu_{\\hat E}$."

STALE_QUOTE pthm-td-finite-bath-canonical-error/boundary empty: items/pthm-td-finite-bath-canonical-error.md Statement; expected "Let the subsystem have a finite nonempty state set $\Omega$ and internal energies $E_x$ in joules with $|E_x|\le L$. A bath has a dimensionless shell entropy $s_B(u)$, defined on an open interval containing $[u_0-L,u_0+L]$ in joules, with $s_B\in C^2$ and $|s_B''(u)|\le M$ there; the model adopts $\beta=s'_B(u_0)>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$ and $T=(k_{\mathrm B}\beta)^{-1}$. Assume weak additive coupling and microcanonical shell sampling induce subsystem weights $P_B(x)\propto e^{s_B(u_0-E_x)}$. Let $P_C(x)=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ be the corresponding canonical law. With $\delta=ML^2/2$ (dimensionless), the shell log-weight remainder obeys
$$|s_B(u_0-E_x)-s_B(u_0)+\beta E_x|\le\delta,$$
and the normalized laws satisfy
$$\sum_{x\in\Omega}|P_B(x)-P_C(x)|\le e^{2\delta}-1.$$
This is an $\ell^1$ probability-vector bound; it does not assert a universal error or a thermodynamic limit."

STALE_QUOTE def-td-driven-finite-path-model/boundary nonempty-choice: items/def-td-driven-finite-path-model.md Definition; expected "Take $\Omega$ to be a finite nonempty microstate set as in [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: distinct elements count as distinct microstates, and the physical energy values are finite and measured in joules in the declared rest frame. Fix an integer $m\ge1$ and stage energy functions $E_k:\Omega\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ for $k=0,\ldots,m$, with the energy offsets fixed by the declared protocol model. Fix inverse temperature $\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$. The finite partition sum and canonical probability vector at stage $k$ are $Z_k=\sum_{i\in\Omega}e^{-\beta E_k(i)}$ and $\pi_k(i)=e^{-\beta E_k(i)}/Z_k$. Since $\Omega$ is nonempty and finite and each energy is finite, $0<Z_k<\infty$ and $\pi_k$ is a strictly positive probability vector.

A transition kernel at stage $k$ is a matrix $K_k(i,j)\ge0$ with $\sum_{j\in\Omega}K_k(i,j)=1$. In the forward stage order, the energy changes instantaneously from $E_{k-1}$ to $E_k$ while the state is still $i_{k-1}$; the subsequent bath transition samples $i_k$ using $K_k(i_{k-1},i_k)$ at fixed energy $E_k$. A path is $\omega=(i_0,\ldots,i_m)\in\Omega^{m+1}$. For an initial law $\mu_0$, its path probability is $P_F(\omega)=\mu_0(i_0)\prod_{k=1}^mK_k(i_{k-1},i_k)$.

Work on the system is positive when energy is supplied to it, and heat into the system is positive when a bath transition raises its energy. Define $W(\omega)=\sum_{k=1}^m[E_k(i_{k-1})-E_{k-1}(i_{k-1})]$ and $Q_{\mathrm{in}}(\omega)=\sum_{k=1}^m[E_k(i_k)-E_k(i_{k-1})]$, both in joules. Define $F_k=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_k$ and $\Delta F=F_m-F_0=-\beta^{-1}\log(Z_m/Z_0)$. These are finite-model quantities; their physical interpretation is conditional on the adopted preparation and transition assumptions."
